cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at time complexity of merge sort.
So we have said that when we are sorting the array using merge first we are dividing it into two parts.
Then we are dividing it these arrays into two parts.
And it continues like this until we reach the one element.
Now we have eight elements over here, and it took three steps to divide it until the end.
So this means that two to the power of three is going to be eight.
And this is all log n time complexity.
Now we have to find out the time complexity for dividing this array until we reach the one element.
Now we need to combine it.
Now when we combine this we have to loop through these arrays one by one to be able to combine them.
So this means that this is going to take on time complexity.
Now if we combine everything together it's going to be on log n time complexity.
Now when it comes to the space complexity here, we need the additional space for dividing this array
into two parts and store it in the memory.
So when we divide it into two parts we will have new space.
And it continues like this.
So this means that every time when we are dividing the array we need an additional space.
And at the end we will have the n number of arrays over here.
So that's why the space complexity for merge sort is going to be o n.
So the time complexity is o n log n and the space complexity is o n.
